findings.summary: The Cost javadoc says "these accessors exist only to make the failure message readable" two lines before saying the accessors are gone; the record has only delta().
findings.detail: Lines 171-172 end the first paragraph with "the test compares the entire delta and these accessors exist only to make the failure message readable", and lines 174-180 then say "AND THE ACCESSORS ARE GONE" and record that reads()/puts() were measured dead by construction. The record at line 182 is `private record Cost(StoreCounts delta)` -- there are no accessors beyond the single component, so the first sentence is false as it stands and the two paragraphs contradict each other. Failure scenario: whoever extends this pin for a new request kind (M5.6g's sweep is explicitly handed off in this same file) reads the first paragraph, goes looking for the reads()/puts() helpers it says exist, and either re-adds them -- restoring exactly the four dead-by-construction assertions round 4 measured and removed -- or concludes the javadoc describes a different file and stops trusting it. Related and in the same place: with the accessors gone, Cost is a single-component wrapper over StoreCounts that forwardedCommitCost could return directly. Per review.md rule 11 this belongs in the commit body, not in a sixth round -- the surface a fix would add is more of the prose that is already the defect.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever extends this pin for a new request kind -- M5.6g's sweep is handed off in this very file -- reads line 171's "these accessors exist only to make the failure message readable", goes looking for reads()/puts(), and either re-adds them, restoring exactly the four dead-by-construction assertions round 4 measured and removed, or concludes the javadoc describes a different file and stops trusting the rest of it.
